MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of marine and freshwater environments? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio? (1 mark)

   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

19. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)

   B. Primary consumers only

   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.
